sections.title: Cosmic Beginning, Causation, and a Personal Creator
sections.rationale: This opening section contains the cosmological case and the ensuing exchange over an absolute beginning, creation from nothing, actual infinities, and whether a nonphysical cause may be identified as a mind. Its weight reflects the number and structural breadth of the distinct cosmological steps and replies.

moveAssignments.rationale: This is the section's foundational constructive route from a finite cosmic beginning to an uncaused, timeless, spaceless, and immaterial transcendent cause.
This extends the cosmological route from a nonphysical transcendent cause to an unembodied mind and personal creator.
This is a major reply addressing whether ordinary causal experience supports extending causation to creation from nothing.
This supplies the principal scientific challenge to inferring an absolute cosmic beginning from expansion and current physical theory.
This directly contests the inference from a nonphysical cosmic cause to an unembodied mind or other familiar category.
This is the principal reply defending the beginning inference through the stated scope and implications of the Borde-Guth-Vilenkin theorem.
This directly answers the creation-from-nothing objection by distinguishing material causes from efficient causes.
This develops a supporting mathematical objection to the claim that infinite subtraction establishes a contradiction in reality.
This supplies the corresponding counterreply about translating nonunique infinite subtraction into a real collection of objects.

sections.title: Fine-Tuning, Alternative Explanations, and Divine Specificity
sections.rationale: This section follows the fine-tuning exchange from the initial design inference through a conditional concession, probability and multiverse cautions, the specificity objection, Craig's reply, and his later limitation concerning infinite power. The weight represents a distinct evidential line with several independent structural questions.

moveAssignments.rationale: This is the load-bearing fine-tuning construction comparing physical necessity, chance, and design as explanations.
This conditional concession identifies the evidential circumstances under which cosmic fine-tuning would invite a designer explanation.
This is the main skeptical reply concerning purpose detection, probability from one universe, deeper physics, and multiverse alternatives.
This adds the major specificity issue that a life-permitting universe does not by itself identify a morally perfect Christian God.
This consolidates the principal reply on parameter ranges, future physics, multiple fine-tuning cases, and the separate moral route.
This material concession marks the stated limit of what fine-tuning and the presented arguments establish about divine power.

sections.title: Objective Morality, Divine Goodness, and the Evidence of Evil
sections.rationale: This section begins with the moral argument, then groups the exchange over atheistic moral realism, moral grounding, the empirical problem of evil, and a purposive theistic reply. Its weight reflects the section's dual role in the positive moral case and the contrary evidential case concerning a perfect God.

moveAssignments.rationale: This is the section's load-bearing constructive route from objective moral values to God as their necessary ground.
This directly challenges the claimed dependence of objective morality and intrinsic human value on God's existence.
This answers the atheistic morality challenge by focusing on nonarbitrary value and the source of binding moral obligation.
This is the load-bearing contrary empirical route from observed evil and purported divine morality to skepticism about a perfect God.
This is the principal reply proposing a divine purpose for permitting natural and moral evil in human history.

sections.title: Resurrection Evidence and the Gospel Sources
sections.rationale: This section isolates the historical resurrection inference and the direct exchange over the dating, authorship, dependence, discrepancies, and scholarly acceptance of its central facts. Its weight reflects a separate route to specifically Christian theism with a compact but complete constructive-objection-reply sequence.

moveAssignments.rationale: This is the section's load-bearing construction from the empty tomb, appearances, and disciples' belief to resurrection and God's existence.
This is the principal historical-source challenge concerning authorship, dependence, advocacy purposes, and discrepancies among the Gospel accounts.
This directly replies by locating the three cited facts within the stated majority view and the positions of skeptical scholars.

sections.title: Religious Experience, Competing Religions, and the Overall Burden
sections.rationale: This final topical section begins with personal religious experience and includes the challenge from conflicting religions, the reply about methods, the skeptical prior-burden construction, and the response concerning expected evidence. Its weight reflects its role in connecting experiential evidence and hypothesis comparison to the debate-wide cumulative routes.

moveAssignments.rationale: This is the load-bearing experiential construction that presents immediate awareness of God as a route independent of argument.
This is the principal reply arguing that similar belief-forming sources yield incompatible religions and therefore require caution.
This states the skeptical route's debate-wide hypothesis comparison and the proposed burden for the specific Christian God.
This directly answers the religious-diversity challenge by distinguishing methods and identifying logic, evidence, and experience.
This addresses the overall skeptical burden by disputing the expectation that God's existence would produce more observable evidence.

bridgeMappings.rationale: The five retained constructive moves occupy the five topical sections and collectively preserve the complete motion-level evidential route from cosmology, fine-tuning, morality, resurrection, and religious experience.
These retained moves distribute the cumulative evidential lines and later replies across all five sections, preserving the central convergence route and its engagement with the skeptical comparison.

Section 01 retains the beginning-and-cause construction, the personal-cause extension, and the replies concerning cosmological evidence, causation, and actual infinity that represent this subsidiary bridge.
Section 02 retains both the original comparison among necessity, chance, and design and the later reply concerning probability ranges, future physics, and the division of work among arguments.
Section 04 retains the three-fact resurrection construction and the later defense of those facts through the stated historical consensus and skeptical scholars' positions.
The retained moves in Sections 03 and 05 state the contrary empirical case from evil and the debate-wide hypothesis-comparison burden, together preserving the skeptical motion-level route.

These retained moves distribute the underdetermination, alternative-explanation, specificity, conflicting-religion, and source-evidence challenges across every topical section of the skeptical central route.

Section 01 retains the challenges to causal extrapolation, an absolute beginning, identification of a nonphysical cause as mind, and the actual-infinity argument that jointly represent this subsidiary route.
Section 02 retains the conditional concession, the probability and alternative-explanation cautions, and the objection that fine-tuning does not identify an omniperfect Christian God.
Section 03 retains the explicit empirical comparison between the observed world, purported divine morality, and the expectations associated with a morally perfect Christian God.
